descriptionChirho: Negative coordinating conjunction joining clauses or items under negation, equivalent to 'and not' or 'nor', continuing a preceding negative. The dominant usage (55 of 58 occurrences). S72379 and S72380 share identical translation signatures: eng 'nor', spa 'ni/tampoco', hin न/न ही, arb ولا, kor 또한/~도 말고, swa 'wala'. The split between them is artificial -- both represent the same simple negative coordination function with no distinguishable semantic difference in any language.

Emphatic negative particle meaning 'not even', intensifying the negation beyond simple coordination to express that something surprising or extreme is also excluded. Multilingual evidence diverges clearly from the plain 'nor' cluster: eng 'not even/Not even', spa 'ni siquiera' (emphatic form), kor 조차/심지어 아니 ('even/not even'), swa 'hata si-' ('even not'). The Spanish 'ni siquiera', Korean 조차, and Swahili 'hata si-' all employ emphatic scalar particles absent from the plain 'nor' translations.
